All 3 failures confirm the same underlying bug, and all other 26 tests pass as expected.

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/LexerAgentTest.java` (JUnit 4, matching the project's existing test style), testing `Lexer`'s package-private behavior through the concrete `CSVLexer` subclass: constructor field wiring, `getLineNumber`, `readEscape` (named/literal control chars, meta-char pass-through, EOF error), `trimTrailingSpaces`, `readEndOfLine` (CRLF/LF/CR/non-EOL), `isWhitespace`, `isStartOfLine`, `isEndOfFile`, and `isDelimiter`/`isEscape`/`isQuoteChar`/`isCommentStart`.

29 tests run, 3 fail, all pointing to the same bug:

- **`testDisabledEscapeDoesNotMatchSentinelCharacter`**
- **`testDisabledQuoteCharDoesNotMatchSentinelCharacter`**
- **`testDisabledCommentStartDoesNotMatchSentinelCharacter`**

**Bug:** `Lexer` uses the sentinel char `'\ufffe'` (`DISABLED`) internally to mean "this feature (escape/quote/comment) is turned off" (`Lexer.java:42`, `mapNullToDisabled`). But `isEscape`, `isQuoteChar`, and `isCommentStart` just compare the input character against that field with no awareness that it's a sentinel. If the character `'\ufffe'` ever actually appears in the input data while the corresponding feature is disabled, `isEscape('\ufffe')`/`isQuoteChar('\ufffe')`/`isCommentStart('\ufffe')` incorrectly return `true`, even though the user never configured any such character. The class comment justifying the sentinel choice is also factually wrong — it claims `U+FFFE` "would be encoded as two chars (using surrogates)", but `U+FFFE` is in the Basic Multilingual Plane and is represented as a single `char` in Java, so no such collision avoidance actually holds.

The other 26 tests pass and reflect intended, documented behavior.
